name: posix_fadvise
synopsis: int posix_fadvise(int fd, off_t offset, off_t len, int advice);
description: posix_fadvise() allows programs to announce an intended access pattern for a file region, enabling kernel optimizations. It applies to a specified offset and length in the file, but the advice is not binding and serves only as an expectation.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the file to advise.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Starting offset of the region to advise.

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the region, or 0 to indicate until the end of the file.

parameters.name: advice
parameters.description: Advice type, such as POSIX_FADV_NORMAL, indicating the access pattern.

return_value.failure: Returns an error number on error

errors.description: The fd argument was not a valid file descriptor.
An invalid value was specified for advice.
The specified file descriptor refers to a pipe or FIFO.

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.6, if len was specified as 0, it was interpreted as zero bytes instead of meaning all bytes through to the end of the file.
versions: Kernel support since Linux 2.5.60; glibc since 2.2
